text:
jess: Quick sync — I'm proposing we unify the eviction "signals" from the KV layer and the prefix cache into a single lifecycle API. Current situation is messy: two separate paths, duplicated backoff logic, and subtle races when tombstones are emitted.

ravi: +1 to cleaning it up. sketch out what the single API would expose?

matt: TL;DR: a small orthogonal surface that emits explicit lifecycle events (ADMIT, SOFT_EVICT, HARD_EVICT, TOUCH, STALE_MARK) with optional metadata: reason, epoch, origin-node.

olivia: Curious about ordering semantics. Do we guarantee monotonic epochs? What about re-admit after SOFT_EVICT while HARD_EVICT in-flight?

jess: Good Q. Proposal: every prefix/tenant has an epoch number. lifecycle events include epoch and a monotonic seq. Handlers must compare (epoch, seq) to decide no-ops. Re-admit after SOFT_EVICT increments seq but keeps epoch. HARD_EVICT bumps epoch (invalidates older seqs).

sam: How does this play with tombstones? We saw a bug where a tombstone was written but the prefix was later rehydrated on another node and kept stale data.

matt: We should attach a tombstone-token to SOFT_EVICT/HARD_EVICT. The token is included in any write that compacts/clears the keyspace. If a node tries to rehydrate and its token doesn't match latest, it rejects the rehydrate.

ravi: That helps. But adding tokens means more metadata per prefix. Cost?
jess: Token is tiny (8 bytes), and only stored on the lease record; not in every KV. Overhead negligible compared to correctness benefit.

olivia: Operator experience: how do we debug when an item is stuck in limbo? We need deterministic traces.
matt: lifecycle events should be emitted to telemetry with trace IDs. Also provide an API to query latest (epoch, seq, token) for a prefix. That lets support dump exact state.

sam: Race scenarios — imagine node A soft-evicts then node B prefetches with old token, then A hard-evicts. B tries to serve a request before it sees HARD_EVICT. We need graceful rejection path that falls back to origin model or shadow read.
jess: Yes — handler contract: if rehydrate or read sees token mismatch, return STALE_REJECT and optionally start async rehydrate from authoritative owner. We shouldn't return stale data.

ravi: What about batching and continuous batching optimizations? We depend on fast negative responses for fallback. Adding token checks could add a branch in the hot path. Will we regress p99?
matt: Microbenchmark showed token compare is a single integer compare on the lease path, not per-token. For most hot reads we avoid lease lookup because of prefix pin. But when lease check happens it's cheap. We should still benchmark on the hotpath cluster.

olivia: Rollouts: how to migrate? We have many nodes with current behavior.
jess: Migration plan: 1) Add read-only emission of lifecycle events (non-enforced) + telemetry. 2) Deploy observer that flags anomalies and rehydrate-rejects. 3) Flip opt-in enforcement per-region. 4) Global enforcement and retire old paths.

sam: Backward-compat: Dedicated customers pinned to old runtime — opt-in toggle per-deployment.
ravi: One more edge: multi-tenant slabs where eviction fairness policy triggers cross-tenant demote. Lifecycle API must carry a hint (fairness-priority) so allocator can make better decisions.
matt: We can add 'hint_priority' optional enum to SOFT_EVICT events. It won't change correctness, just inputs for allocator.

olivia: Any implications for durability and crash-recovery? Lease state must be persisted atomically with eviction intent, or we get split-brain.
jess: Persist lease record with (epoch, token, seq) in a strongly-consistent store (we already have one for metadata). Eviction intent log is append-only for audit.

sam: Tests? We need property tests that inject reorderings, drops, and simulate rehydrate after tombstone. Also e2e: simulate cold-rehydrate when hard-evict concurrent.
matt: I'll sketch a harness: random epoch bumps, delayed HARD_EVICT, then attempt rehydrate on a delayed node and assert STALE_REJECT until re-sync.
ravi: One UX ask: surface historical lifecycle events in Console per-prefix timeline. Helps debug cross-region tears.
jess: Agreed — Console will show last N events with traces. Also an endpoint for reconcile actions.

olivia: Any open risks?
sam: Biggest risk is subtle races during cutover. We'll need a canary with single shard. Also watch p99 during opt-in.
matt: Ops knobs: graceful backoff window after SOFT_EVICT during which reads degrade to shadow-read vs immediate reject. Keep it configurable.
jess: Action items: matt -> PR with lifecycle proto and small bench (due EOW). ravi -> migration plan doc for Dedicated and Hosted (sync tomorrow). olivia -> Console skeleton for event timeline (POC next week). sam -> test harness seed cases. I'll add a small RFC summary to the rfc repo after the sync.
deploy-bot: Deployment reminder: matt's bench cluster scheduled Tue 02:00 UTC.

jess: Thanks all. If no major objections I'll start the opt-in telemetry patch today.
ravi: No objections from me. :thumbsup:

olivia: Looks good.
matt: On it.
sam: Thanks.
